title: Design a Ticket Booking System (BookMyShow)
subtitle: Distributed seat locks, Redis TTL reservations, and flash-sale queue management

stages.title: Stage 1 — RDBMS Row Locks
stages.bottleneck: During blockbuster movie release (100,000 users selecting seat A1 simultaneously), database `SELECT FOR UPDATE` causes row lock contention & deadlock crashes.
stages.narrative: **Database Row Locks.** RDBMS pessimistic locking on seat rows prevents double booking, but database connection pools blow up under 100K flash sale users.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Redis Temporary Distributed Seat Holds (10-Min TTL)
stages.bottleneck: If a user locks a seat and abandons payment, the seat remains locked forever without automated expiry.
stages.narrative:
**Distributed Redis Seat Holding.** Seat reservation uses Redis atomic `SETNX` (Set if Not Exists) with a 10-minute expiration TTL.

If payment succeeds within 10 minutes, convert to permanent DB booking. If payment fails/times out, Redis TTL key naturally expires, releasing the seat instantly for other buyers.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Virtual Waiting Room & Queue Throttling
stages.bottleneck: Surge traffic crashing ticket servers during Coldplay concert booking.
stages.narrative: **Virtual Waiting Room & Rate Throttling.** Excess traffic is held in a virtual queue with a visual position number (e.g. "You are #4,102 in line"). Only a calibrated rate of users enter the seat map selection page.
